entries.summary: CLI, Shared/Core, SDK changes across 6 file(s) (+704/−110).

ai.title: Sponsored Linux worktree git sandbox rebased on tmpfs
ai.summary: The CLI's sponsored-run containment for linked git worktrees now mounts the user's real `.git` common dir as a tmpfs with its entries rebound read-only, instead of binding it read-only and covering dangerous paths. `prepareLinkedWorktreeForLinux` makes the run's own branch loose from `packed-refs` and creates the namespace directories the writable binds need, and `HIDDEN_COMMON_DIR_ENTRIES` keeps `packed-refs` and `packed-refs.lock` out of the bounce so git can take its lock while a packed-ref table rewrite is never reachable on the host. This is the Linux arm of `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts`, which is shared by the CLI via `cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts`.
ai.evidence: In `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts`, `linkedWorktreeBindArgs` (read-only common dir with read-only overlays) is replaced by `prepareLinkedWorktreeForLinux`, which mounts an empty `--tmpfs` at the common dir, rebinds every existing entry read-only via `linuxCommonDirMounts`, and deliberately omits `packed-refs` and `packed-refs.lock` via `HIDDEN_COMMON_DIR_ENTRIES`; `spawnLinux` now calls `prepareLinkedWorktreeForLinux` and binds the granted write subpaths writable on top.
ai.unknowns: The new test gate's integration into the CLI/Desktop suites and the ci.yml test-sponsored-containment job are not shown in this diff, and the consumer of the Auth pair's campaign ids in the serving path is not visible here.

changes.what: Rebased the Linux linked-worktree git sandbox on a tmpfs of the common dir with entries rebound read-only, replacing the previous read-only bind and per-path overlays; added prepareLinkedWorktreeForLinux, linuxCommonDirMounts, HIDDEN_COMMON_DIR_ENTRIES, and the --tmpfs flag.

Reworked upstream refusal handling in acceptSponsoredProposal: enumerated PROPOSAL_ERROR_SENTENCES (funded_accept_required, invalid_state, cloud_keyed), added looksLikeMachineCode, and rewrote upstreamMessage so known codes map to human sentences while unknown prose still surfaces; read_files.

Wired the typed OverrideToolHandlers into the sponsored turn: sponsoredOverrideTools now returns SponsoredOverrideTools (the seven admitted tools, all required) and runSponsoredTurn passes it without a `never` cast.

Added the Supabase format-pair registry: SUPABASE_FORMAT_DATABASE_PAIR (supabase-database-persist-one-feature@1.1.0) and SUPABASE_FORMAT_AUTH_PROCEDURE, plus supabaseFormatPairs/parseSupabaseAuthFormatCampaignIds reading FREEBUFF_SUPABASE_AUTH_FORMAT_CAMPAIGN_IDS and the pair lookup helpers.
Exported OverrideToolHandlers as a public SDK type alongside the existing run/run-state exports.

Added the shared containment test gate (sponsoredContainmentUsable, sponsoredContainmentTestGate) that skips when no sandbox host is present and fails the build under SPONSORED_CONTAINMENT_REQUIRED=1.

ai.title: Add updateRequired flag for legacy Desktop clients
ai.summary: Introduced `updateRequired` boolean to `FreebuffSessionAdmissionResponse` and helper functions in `freebuff-models.ts`. Signals legacy Desktop binaries cannot resume purchased time due to client version, not model failure. Prevents misleading 'model unavailable' errors by scoping refusal to client update. Only affects Desktop multi-session path; older clients ignore flag but render updated availability label.

eli5.text: The Freebuff Desktop app now gets a clearer message when an old version can't resume a purchased hour: instead of being told the model is unavailable, you're told your app version needs updating and that doing so won't charge you again. This only affects the Desktop multi-session path, for binaries old enough to lack a purchase-rotation mechanism; newer clients and web users see the existing availability labels unchanged. The server sets the new flag and, for supported clients, surfaces the updated wording, while older binaries continue rendering the generic label (worded so it doesn't blame the model). It's live today for any Desktop binary new enough to read the flag.

ai.title: Thinker-gemini moves to GPT-5.6 Luna with xhigh reasoning
ai.summary: The freebuff.com/chat thinker agent (id `thinker-gemini`) now runs on `FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID` instead of the DeepSeek V4 Flash constant, and its `reasoningOptions.effort` moves from `high` to `xhigh`, reflecting the prior cost-driven move off Gemini 3.1 Pro. Reasoning is declared explicitly rather than left to the catalog default, since a thinker that does not think is just a slower copy of the root agent. The `AgentDefinition`, initial-agents-dir template copy, backend `OpenRouterReasoningOptions`, and `DynamicAgentDefinitionSchema` reasoning enum all add `max` and `xhigh` to the allowed `effort` tiers.
ai.evidence: thinker-gemini.ts imports FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID instead of FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL_ID, sets model to that constant, and changes reasoningOptions.effort from 'high' to 'xhigh'; the three type files widen the effort union/ zod enum from 'high' | 'medium' | 'low' | 'minimal' | 'none' to also include 'max' | 'xhigh'
ai.migration: If you authored a custom agent relying on the prior `reasoningOptions.effort` values of only high, medium, low, minimal, or none, your template still validates unchanged, but new agents can now opt into max or xhigh.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show where `FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID` is defined or published, or whether GPT-5.6 Luna is a free-tier model, so the user-facing cost/availability implications are not visible here.
